name: Bisoprolol
summary: A highly beta-1-selective blocker commonly used when a clean, once-daily cardioselective beta blocker is wanted.
good: Cardiac rate control or heart-failure regimens where beta-1 selectivity is preferred.
bad: Severe bradycardia or active decompensation without specialist direction.
clinicalPearls: Its strong beta-1 selectivity is the reason clinicians often describe it as a clean cardiac beta blocker.
mechanism: Selective beta-1 blockade lowers heart rate and renin release.
indications: Hypertension and heart failure, especially where a simple once-daily regimen helps adherence.
interactionNotes: Other rate-lowering drugs and severe conduction disease are the main practical concerns.

warnings: Bradycardia, fatigue, dizziness, and masked hypoglycemia symptoms can occur.
